summary: GRI 201 covers the organization's economic performance and how it manages related impacts. It addresses economic value generated and distributed, defined benefit plan obligations, government financial assistance, and the financial implications of climate change.

questions.text: Describe the actual and potential, negative and positive impacts of the organization on the economy, environment and people, including impacts on their human rights, in relation to economic performance.
questions.hint: Describe the actual and potential, negative and positive impacts on the economy, environment, and people, including impacts on human rights (GRI 3-3-a).

questions.text: State whether the organization is involved with the negative impacts related to economic performance through its own activities or as a result of its business relationships, and describe how.
questions.hint: Say whether the organization causes or contributes to the negative impacts through its activities, or whether they are linked to its operations, products or services through business relationships, and describe how (GRI 3-3-b).

questions.text: Describe the organization's policies or commitments regarding economic performance.
questions.hint: Describe policies or commitments regarding the material topic (GRI 3-3-c).

questions.text: Describe the actions taken to manage economic performance and the related impacts.
questions.hint: Include: i. how negative impacts are prevented or mitigated; ii. how actual negative impacts are addressed, including actions to provide for or cooperate in remediation; iii. how actual and potential positive impacts are managed (GRI 3-3-d).

questions.text: How does the organization track the effectiveness of its actions on economic performance?
questions.hint: Report: i. information about the effectiveness of the actions; ii. the goals, targets and indicators used to evaluate progress; iii. lessons learned and how they have been integrated into policies and operational procedures (GRI 3-3-e).

questions.text: Describe how engagement with stakeholders has informed the actions taken on economic performance and whether those actions have been effective.
questions.hint: Describe how stakeholder engagement has informed the actions taken (3-3-d) and how it has informed whether the actions have been effective (3-3-e) (GRI 3-3-f).

disclosures.title: Direct economic value generated and distributed

questions.text: What direct economic value did the organization generate, distribute and retain, on an accruals basis?
questions.hint: Report EVG&D on an accruals basis for global operations: i. direct economic value generated (revenues); ii. economic value distributed (operating costs, employee wages and benefits, payments to providers of capital, payments to government by country, community investments); iii. economic value retained (generated less distributed). If data are on a cash basis, justify the decision.

questions.text: Where significant, what is the economic value generated and distributed at country, regional or market level, and what criteria define significance?
questions.hint: Report EVG&D separately at country, regional or market levels where significant, and the criteria used for defining significance.

disclosures.title: Financial implications and other risks and opportunities due to climate change

questions.text: Which risks and opportunities posed by climate change could generate substantive changes in your operations, revenue or expenditure?
questions.hint: For each: i. description and classification (physical, regulatory or other); ii. the associated impact; iii. financial implications before action is taken; iv. methods used to manage it; v. costs of actions taken to manage it.

disclosures.title: Defined benefit plan obligations and other retirement plans

questions.text: If the plan's liabilities are met by the organization's general resources, what is the estimated value of those liabilities?
questions.hint: Estimated value of the defined benefit plan liabilities met from general resources.

questions.text: If a separate fund exists to pay the plan's pension liabilities, to what extent are they covered by the assets set aside?
questions.hint: i. Extent to which liabilities are estimated to be covered by assets set aside; ii. basis on which the estimate was arrived at; iii. when the estimate was made.

questions.text: If the fund is not fully covered, what strategy and timescale does the employer have to reach full coverage?
questions.hint: Explain the strategy, if any, to work towards full coverage and the timescale, if any, by which full coverage is expected.

questions.text: What percentage of salary is contributed by the employee or the employer?
questions.hint: Percentage of salary contributed by employee or employer.

questions.text: What is the level of participation in retirement plans?
questions.hint: Participation in mandatory or voluntary schemes, regional or country-based schemes, or those with financial impact.

questions.text: What is the total monetary value of financial assistance received from any government during the reporting period?
questions.hint: Include: i. tax relief and tax credits; ii. subsidies; iii. investment, R&D and other grants; iv. awards; v. royalty holidays; vi. Export Credit Agency assistance; vii. financial incentives; viii. other financial benefits received or receivable from any government for any operation.

questions.text: What is the financial assistance received from government, broken down by country?
Is any government present in the shareholding structure and, if so, to what extent?
questions.hint: Whether, and the extent to which, any government is present in the shareholding structure.
